concept.name: Premium zone
concept.definition: In SMC/ICT vocabulary, the upper half of a 'dealing range' — the leg between a significant swing low and swing high — i.e., everything above the 50% midpoint. The convention frames longs taken in premium as poor value and shorts in premium as acceptable value; it is a positioning heuristic, not a valuation measure.
concept.intuition: Split the range in half; buying in the top half means paying up relative to where the market has just been.
concept.mechanics: Anchor the dealing range at a meaningful swing low and high; the midpoint is equilibrium and the region above it is premium. SMC models look for sell-side setups (bearish order blocks, bearish FVGs) located in premium, aligned with the higher-timeframe bias.
concept.formula: Equilibrium = (range high + range low) / 2; premium zone = prices above that midpoint within the dealing range.
concept.failure_modes: In strong trends price lives in premium for long stretches, so 'expensive' stays expensive; the framework also depends entirely on which swing anchors are chosen.
concept.misconceptions: That premium means overvalued in any fundamental sense; it is purely a relative position within one analyst-chosen range.
concept.example: With a dealing range of 1800-1900, equilibrium sits at 1850; a bearish order block at 1875 lies in premium, qualifying it — under SMC convention — as a short-entry zone.
